eval-bot: nightly-eval: Quality spike detected on 1709456789 for model@v2-int8 (promptset: multi-turn-docs). metric: duplicate_snippet_rate up 6.3x vs baseline :warning:

maria: saw this in dashboard, looks like duplicates at end of turn echos, often with footnotes. pulling sample set now.

kevin: can you paste a few failing examples?

maria: sure, two short excerpts:
```
User: Summarize section 3 with footnote refs.
Model: ... result text ...[1][1][1]
```
```
User: Explain table values.
Model: ... see note a. see note a. see note a.
```

sophie: interesting - this started after the bpe-v2 tokenizer + int8 bundle we rolled last week, right?

maria: timeline matches. nightly started using model@v2-int8+bpe-v2 on 1709380000. before that baseline (v2-fp16+bpe-v1) had duplicate_snippet_rate ~0.5%. now it's 3.2%.

ashwin: hypothesis: tokenization change shifts merge boundaries for bracketed footnotes and the int8 KV/decoding path + prefix cache combine to produce repeated decode loops for specific suffix tokens.

kevin: can we reproduce locally with the failing promptset? steps?

maria: reproduction steps I used:
1) checkout model bundle `release/v2-int8-bpev2`
2) run `python eval/run_promptset.py --model model.bin --tokenizer bpe-v2 --promptset multi-turn-docs --seed 42 --out failures.json`
3) look for repeated token sequences with regex `([\w\]\[]+)\1{2,}`

kevin: ran it, reproduced 12/200 samples. attaching a snippet of tokenized sequences:
```
Input tokens: [..., 102, 358, 5, 9]
Output tokens: [..., 102, 358, 102, 358, 102, 358]
```

ashwin: that pattern says model emitted the same token subsequence repeatedly. two possible causes: decoder loop (score oscillation) or KV cache misalignment so the decoder sees prefix as new context each step.

ashwin: i instrumented decoder logs with `--trace-kv` and see repeated cache keys for positions where bpe-v2 splits the footnote marker into different token IDs vs bpe-v1. kv-index mapping drifted when we apply packed-kv-stride optimization in int8 runtime.

maria: put short excerpt of kv trace (redacted):
```
step 48: key_hash=0x1a2b3c id_seq=[... 102,358]
step 49: key_hash=0x1a2b3c id_seq=[... 102,358]
step 50: key_hash=0x1a2b3c id_seq=[... 102,358]
```

kevin: that looks like the runtime is returning the same logits because it thinks the prefix hasn't advanced, which would cause repetition. Could bpe-v2 token length change interact with packed-kv stride math?

ashwin: yes. packed-kv-stride assumes stable token id sequences for alignment; changing tokenizer merges changes token lengths and off-by-one in stride window leads to repeated key reuse. int8 quant pack kernels also use smaller accumulator windows which amplify the effect.

sophie: root cause summary (draft): bpe-v2 changed merge boundaries for bracketed/footnote tokens leading to altered token lengths; combined with packed-kv-stride optimization in the int8 runtime this produced KV index alignment drift so the decoder saw identical KV entries across consecutive steps, producing repeated subsequence emissions.

maria: mitigation proposal (short-term): rollback tokenizer to bpe-v1 for model@v2-int8 in hosted canary and pause rollouts until fix. also disable packed-kv-stride for int8 runtime for this model. update CI gating to detect >1.5% duplicate_snippet_rate.

kevin: ops steps:
- run quick rollback: deploy `model@v2-int8+bpe-v1` to canary (2 nodes) with weight 5%
- set disable flag `packed_kv_stride=false` for int8 runtime for canary
- add alert rule in nightly-eval: if duplicate_snippet_rate > 1.5% block release and notify #eng-ml

ashwin: longer-term fixes:
- adjust packed-kv-stride math to handle variable token-length encodings (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/492)
- add tokenizer-compat tests to model bundle onboarding (compare token alignment patterns between tokenizers and fail if high mismatch)
- extend nightly eval to include targeted footnote/markup cases

sophie: agreed. also assign owners and tickets:
- RLW-482: rollback & canary (owner: kevin)
- RLW-483: runtime stride fix & unit tests (owner: ashwin)
- RLW-484: gating rule + eval set extension (owner: maria)

maria: timeline: rollback to canary within 1h, monitor for 6h. if metrics return to baseline, promote rollback to production and keep runtime fix gated until completed.

kevin: started canary rollback now. deploy job: `deploy/hosted canary model@v2-int8+bpe-v1 --weight 5`

maria: i'm updating the nightly-eval dashboard to highlight duplicate_snippet_rate per prompt bucket and added the new gating rule in the job config (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/221).

eval-bot: alert acknowledged; nightly-eval gating set: duplicate_snippet_rate threshold=1.5% (applied to model@v2-int8 canary).

kevin: canary logs show immediate drop to 0.6% on canary nodes after rollback. monitoring for next batches. :thumbsup:

ashwin: next steps for runtime PR: add vectorized key-hash recompute and a fuzz test with tokenizer permutations. aiming for code review by EOD.

sophie: good work team. will follow up in RLW tickets and mark postmortem if runtime fix takes >72h. :white_check_mark:

maria: adding short blurb for engineering-comms so we can tell customers what happened (root cause + mitigations). will paste draft here for review.

maria: draft for comms:
"We observed elevated duplicate outputs in nightly evals after onboarding a new tokenizer variant (bpe-v2) together with an int8 runtime optimization. Reverting tokenizer for the canary and disabling the optimization resolved the issue. We're rolling out a runtime fix and adding additional onboarding tests and gating rules to prevent recurrence."

ashwin: lgtm.

kevin: lgtm.

sophie: lgtm.

maria: closing thread for daily triage, will reopen if regression resurfaces or runtime PR blocks.
